content: The text provided is a long list of references from various studies, articles, and reports related to HIV/AIDS, its treatment, prevention, and associated interventions. 1. Detailing ethnic differences in HIV disclosure and sexual risk behaviors, a study published in AIDS Care in 2011 (Volume 23, Issue 4, Pages 444–448) explores how cultural and ethnic factors influence the willingness to disclose HIV status and engage in safer sexual practices. 2. Seid M. et al. conducted a study in the Kemissie district of northeast Ethiopia, examining the disclosure of HIV-positive results to sexual partners among adult clinical service users. This research was published in the African Journal of Reproductive Health in 2012 (Volume 16, Issue 1, Pages 97–104). 3. Comer LK et al. investigated the relationship between illness disclosure and mental health among women living with HIV/AIDS. Their findings were published in the Journal of Community & Applied Social Psychology in 2000 (Volume 10, Issue 6, Pages 449–464). 4. Kilewo C. et al. shared experiences from a study on HIV counseling and testing for pregnant women in sub-Saharan Africa, focusing on the prevention of mother-to-child transmission of HIV-1 in Dar es Salaam, Tanzania. This was published in the Journal of Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndromes in 2001 (Volume 28, Issue 5, Pages 458–462). 5. Gari T., Habte D., and Markos E. explored HIV-positive status disclosure among women attending an ART clinic at Hawassa University Referral Hospital in South Ethiopia. Their study appeared in the East African Journal of Public Health in 2010 (Volume 7, Issue 1, Pages 87–91). 6. Holzemer WL et al. presented findings on the impact of HIV stigma on the disclosure of HIV status at the 19th International AIDS Conference in Washington, DC, in 2012 (Abstract THPE437). 7. Rotheram-Borus MJ et al. developed an intervention for parents with AIDS and their adolescent children, which was published in the American Journal of Public Health in 2001 (Volume 91, Pages 1294–1302). 8. Serovich JM et al. conducted a pilot study on an intervention to assist men who have sex with men in disclosing their serostatus to family members. The results were published in AIDS and Behavior in 2011 (Volume 15, Issue 8, Pages 1647–1653). 9. Mundell JP et al. examined the impact of structured support groups for pregnant South African women recently diagnosed as HIV-positive. Their findings were published in Women’s Health in 2011 (Volume 51, Issue 6, Pages 546–565). 10. Otis J et al. evaluated the effects of an empowerment program on the ability of women living with HIV in Mali to manage decisions regarding HIV status disclosure. This was presented at the 19th International AIDS Conference in Washington, DC, in 2012 (Abstract MOPE502). 11. Murphy DA et al. conducted a pilot trial of the TRACK program, a disclosure intervention for HIV-positive mothers. The study was published in the Journal of Consultative Clinical Psychology in 2011 (Volume 79, Issue 2, Pages 203–214). 12. Wolitski RJ, Gomez CA, and Parsons JT assessed the effects of a peer-led behavioral intervention aimed at reducing HIV transmission and promoting serostatus disclosure among HIV-positive gay and bisexual men. This study was published in AIDS in 2005 (Supplement 1, Pages S99–S109). 13. Serovich JM et al. conducted a pilot study on an intervention to help men who have sex with men disclose their serostatus to casual sex partners. The results were published in AIDS Education and Prevention in 2009 (Volume 21, Issue 3, Pages 207–219). 14. Smith-Fawzi MC et al. evaluated a psychosocial support intervention for HIV-affected families in Haiti, with implications for programs and policies for orphans and vulnerable children. This study appeared in Social Science & Medicine in 2012 (Volume 74, Issue 10, Pages 1494–1503). 15. Rotheram-Borus MJ et al. presented the Masihambisane intervention, a peer community health worker program for South African mothers living with HIV, at the 2012 International AIDS Conference in Washington, DC (Abstract WEPE680). 16. Teti M et al. conducted a mixed-methods evaluation of the Protect and Respect intervention, which focused on condom use and disclosure practices among women living with HIV/AIDS. The study was published in AIDS and Behavior in 2010 (Volume 14, Issue 3, Pages 567–579). 17. Dewo Z et al. presented findings on strengthening treatment, care, and support for people living with HIV through community-based treatment services at the 19th International AIDS Conference in Washington, DC, in 2012 (Abstract TUAD0202). 18. Wouters E et al. examined the role of community support in the disclosure of HIV serostatus to family members by public-sector antiretroviral treatment patients in South Africa. This study was published in AIDS Patient Care and STDs in 2009 (Volume 23, Issue 5, Pages 357–364). 19. Olley BO conducted a controlled outcome study on improving well-being through psycho-education among voluntary counseling and testing seekers in Nigeria. The findings were published in AIDS Care in 2006 (Volume 18, Issue 8, Pages 1025–1031). 20. Patterson TL, Shaw WS, and Semple SJ evaluated the outcomes of a randomized controlled trial aimed at reducing sexual risk behaviors among HIV-positive individuals. This study appeared in Annals of Behavioral Medicine in 2003 (Volume 25, Issue 2, Pages 137–145). 21. Chiasson MA et al. reported increased HIV disclosure three months after an online video intervention for men who have sex with men (MSM). The study was published in AIDS Care in 2009 (Volume 21, Issue 9, Pages 1081–1089). 22. The World Health Organization (WHO) provided guidance on couples HIV testing and counseling, including antiretroviral therapy for treatment and prevention in serodiscordant couples, in a 2012 publication. 23. Kabore I et al. evaluated the effect of community-based support services on clinical efficacy and health-related quality of life in HIV/AIDS patients in resource-limited settings in sub-Saharan Africa. This study was published in AIDS Patient Care and STDs in 2010 (Volume 24, Issue 9, Pages 581–594). 24. Fatti G et al. reported improved survival and antiretroviral treatment outcomes in adults receiving community-based adherence support over five years in South Africa. The findings were published in the Journal of Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndromes in 2012 (Volume 61, Issue 4, Pages e50–e58). 25. Grimwood A et al. demonstrated that community adherence support improves program retention in children on antiretroviral treatment in South Africa. This study appeared in the Journal of the International AIDS Society in 2012 (Volume 15, Issue 2, Article 17381). 26. Chang LW et al. evaluated the impact of peer health workers on AIDS care in Rakai, Uganda, through a cluster-randomized trial. The study was published in PLoS One in 2010 (Volume 5, Issue 6, Article e10923). 27. Chang LW et al. assessed the impact of an mHealth intervention for peer health workers on AIDS care in rural Uganda. The findings were published in AIDS and Behavior in 2011 (Volume 15, Issue 8, Pages 1776–1784). 28. Selke HM et al. examined the clinical outcomes of a community-based program in Kenya that shifted antiretroviral delivery from healthcare workers to persons living with HIV/AIDS. This study was published in the Journal of Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndromes in 2010 (Volume 55, Issue 4, Pages 483–490). 29. Simoni JM et al. conducted a randomized controlled trial on peer support and pager messaging to promote antiretroviral therapy adherence in Seattle. The study appeared in the Journal of Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndromes in 2009 (Volume 52, Issue 4, Pages 465–473). 30. Taiwo BO et al. assessed the virologic and adherence benefits of patient-selected HIV treatment partners in resource-limited settings. The findings were published in the Journal of Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndromes in 2010 (Volume 54, Issue 1, Pages 85–92). 31. Futterman D et al. conducted a pilot study combining a cognitive-behavioral intervention and mentor mothers with PMTCT services in South Africa. The study was published in AIDS Care in 2010 (Volume 22, Issue 9, Pages 1093–1100). 32. Talisuna-Alamo S et al. demonstrated that socioeconomic support reduces non-retention in a community-based antiretroviral therapy program in Uganda. This study appeared in the Journal of Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndromes in 2012 (Volume 59, Issue 4, Pages e52–e59). 33. Altice FL et al. showed the superiority of directly administered antiretroviral therapy over self-administered therapy among HIV-infected drug users in a randomized controlled trial. The findings were published in Clinical Infectious Diseases in 2007 (Volume 45, Issue 6, Pages 770–778). 34. Pearson CR et al. conducted a randomized control trial of peer-delivered, modified directly observed therapy for HAART in Mozambique. The study was published in the Journal of Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndromes in 2007 (Volume 46, Issue 2, Pages 238–244). 35. Macalino GE et al. evaluated a community-based directly observed therapy as an adherence intervention for HAART among substance users. The findings were published in AIDS in 2007 (Volume 21, Issue 11, Pages 1473–1477). 36. Igumbor JO et al. assessed the impact of a community-based adherence support program on ART outcomes in selected government HIV treatment sites in South Africa. The study appeared in AIDS Care in 2011 (Volume 23, Issue 2, Pages 231–236). 37. Achieng L et al. compared facilitators of retention in care and adherence to antiretroviral therapy at an HIV treatment center in Kenya. The findings were published in PLoS One in 2012 (Volume 7, Issue 3, Article e32727). 38. Bekker LG et al. reported on the rapid scale-up of a community-based HIV treatment service in Gugulethu, South Africa, over three consecutive years. The study was published in the South African Medical Journal in 2006 (Volume 96, Issue 4, Pages 315–320). 39. Chang LW et al. evaluated two-year virologic outcomes of a peer health worker and nurse-staffed community-based program in Uganda. The findings were published in the Journal of Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndromes in 2009 (Volume 50, Issue 3, Pages 276–282). 40. Kipp W et al. reported results of a community-based antiretroviral treatment program for HIV-1 infection in Western Uganda. The study appeared in Current HIV Research in 2010 (Volume 8, Issue 2, Pages 179–185). 41. Kipp W et al. compared antiretroviral treatment outcomes between a community-based and hospital-based cohort of HIV patients in rural Uganda. The findings were published in BMC International Health and Human Rights in 2011 (Supplement 2, Article S12). 42. Nglazi MD et al. documented changes in programmatic outcomes during seven years of scale-up at a community-based antiretroviral treatment service in South Africa. The study was published in the Journal of Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndromes in 2011 (Volume 56, Issue 1, Pages e1–e8). 43. Nglazi MD et al. evaluated treatment outcomes in HIV-infected adolescents attending a community-based antiretroviral therapy clinic in South Africa. The findings were published in BMC Infectious Diseases in 2012 (Volume 12, Article 21). 44. Rich ML et al. reported excellent clinical outcomes and high retention in care among adults in a community-based HIV treatment program in rural Rwanda. The study appeared in the Journal of Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndromes in 2012 (Volume 59, Issue 3, Pages e35–e42). 45. Stubbs BA et al. examined the role of treatment partners in adherence to HAART in Central Mozambique. The findings were published in AIDS Care in 2009 (Volume 21, Issue 11, Pages 1412–1419). 46. Nan da P et al. evaluated the effectiveness of WHO tools in improving the quality of health services provided by health workers to female clients in India. The study was published by the World Health Organization in 2012. 47. Robling M et al. assessed the impact of the Talking Diabetes consulting skills intervention on glycemic control and quality of life in children with type 1 diabetes. The findings were published in the British Medical Journal in 2012 (April 26; 344: e2359). 48. Gregory J et al. developed and evaluated a psychosocial intervention for children and teenagers with diabetes through a cluster randomized trial. The study was published in Health Technology Assessment in 2011 (Volume 15, Issue 29, Pages 1–202). 49. Lozano P et al. conducted a multisite randomized trial on the effects of physician education and organizational change in chronic asthma care. The study was published in Archives of Pediatrics & Adolescent Medicine in 2004 (Volume 158, Issue 9, Pages 875–883). 50. Shroufi A et al. demonstrated that HIV-infected adolescents in Southern Africa can achieve good treatment outcomes. The findings were published in AIDS in 2013 (Volume 27, Pages 1971–1978). 51. Dewing S et al. evaluated the impact of counseling by lay counselors for ARV adherence support in the Western Cape, South Africa. The study appeared in AIDS and Behavior in 2012 (Volume 17, Issue 1, Pages 203–212). 52. Fisher JD et al. showed that a clinician-delivered intervention during routine clinical care reduces unprotected sexual behavior among HIV-infected patients. The findings were published in the Journal of Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndromes in 2006 (Volume 41, Issue 1, Pages 44–52). 53. Dewing S et al. assessed lay counselors’ fidelity to an evidence-based intervention for promoting antiretroviral adherence in the Western Cape, South Africa. The manuscript was submitted for publication. 54. Dewing S et al. evaluated lay counselors’ ability to deliver counseling for behavior change. The manuscript was submitted for publication. 55. Dewing S et al. conducted a cluster randomized control trial to improve the counseling skills of lay counselors in antiretroviral adherence settings in the Western Cape, South Africa. The manuscript is in preparation. 56. Lewin SA et al. reviewed the role of lay health workers in primary and community healthcare for maternal and child health and the management of infectious diseases. The findings were published in the Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews in 2010 (CD004015). 57. Wong CF et al. examined harassment, discrimination, violence, and illicit drug use among young men who have sex with men. The study was published in AIDS Education and Prevention in 2010 (Volume 22, Pages 286–298). 58. Hurt CB et al. found that sex with older partners is associated with primary HIV infection among men who have sex with men in North Carolina. The study appeared in the Journal of Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndromes in 2010 (Volume 54, Pages 185–190). 59. Koblin BA et al. identified risk factors for HIV infection among men who have sex with men. The study was published in AIDS in 2006 (Volume 20, Pages 731–739). 60. The UNAIDS Inter-Agency Task Team on Education emphasized the importance of HIV and AIDS treatment education as a critical component of efforts to ensure universal access to prevention, treatment, and care. This was published by UNESCO in 2006. 61. Ferrand RA et al. developed a primary care-level algorithm for identifying HIV-infected adolescents in high-risk populations through mother-to-child transmission. The study was published in Tropical Medicine and International Health in 2011 (Volume 16, Pages 349–355). 62. UNICEF, in collaboration with its partners, advocates for and supports effective HIV prevention, treatment, and care for adolescents. This includes efforts to overcome stigma and discrimination and strengthen national responses to fulfill the rights of vulnerable adolescents.
